_source: Balance Bible §11 (economy model) — two resource types with distinct risk/tempo profiles. Both convert to credits; they differ in value-per-load, extraction speed, renewability, and where they sit on the map. Payback for both stays inside the §11 harvester band (100-140 s). Verified by scripts/economy-check.mjs.
_designIntent: Wood is the economic FLOOR — safe, near-base, renewable, low ceiling, hard to fully deny. Ore is the economic CEILING — richer but slower to extract, finite, and parked at contested/expansion points, so it rewards map control and scouting (§12/§13). You want both: wood keeps you alive, ore lets you win.

wood.extraction: fast — short harvest cadence and quick round trips

gatherer.name: Lumber Harvester
gatherer.notes: cheap, quick to build, lightly armored — fast to get a first one running

node.location: near base — the safe, default income
node.regrows: fast — a harvested stand replenishes over time, so wood income is sustainable and hard to permanently deny

wood.role: reliable early trickle and the un-killable economic floor; the resource the harass-and-expand identities (Covenant) can lean on when denied the map

ore.extraction: slow — 'lower to mine'; each load is worth far more but the extraction cadence is deliberate

gatherer.name: Mining Vehicle
gatherer.notes: pricier, slower, better-armored dedicated miner — a real upfront investment, and a fat raid target (§13)

node.location: central + expansion points — contested by design
node.totalCapacity: large but FINITE — a mine depletes and does not come back, so map control over time is a scored resource
node.regrows: none (or very slow) — unlike wood, a mined-out node is gone

ore.role: the economic ceiling and the reason to fight for the map; higher steady value at a secured node, but every credit is gated behind reaching, holding, and defending a contested finite point

tension._note: The two resources create the strategic choice the maps are built around.
tension.woodOnly: survivable but low-ceiling — you will be out-scaled by anyone who also holds ore
tension.oreOnly: high-ceiling but brittle — deny the mine (§13 harassment) or outlast it (finite depletion) and the economy collapses
tension.mixed: the intended play — wood floor + ore ceiling, with the ore contest driving map control and the harassment/comeback loops (§12-14)

oreTechGate._decision: RESOLVED (see design/18-feature-research §3, design/04-economy). Ore is a SOFT tech-gate, NOT a hard second currency. This is the SC2 minerals/gas split: both wood and ore still convert to credits, so a map-denied faction's un-killable wood floor still fields a full tier-1 army and stays alive (§14) — but the tech CEILING is behind the contested resource. Advanced tech requires an ore component; the floor never does.
oreTechGate._model: The single-credit pool from economy.json is preserved for the credit COST of every purchase. Ore is an ADDITIONAL required component layered only on the gated items below — not a parallel currency you must spend on every unit. Wood + ore both refine into the same credit pool; ore additionally unlocks/pays the ore-component on advanced tech.
oreTechGate.rule: tier-1 army and ALL economy (gatherers, refineries, basic static defense) cost credits only and are fully buildable on the wood floor alone. tier-2 and tier-3 production structures, epic-unit tech, the superweapon facility, and the key §18 combat upgrades additionally require an ore component. No ore => you can mass tier-1 basics and survive, but you cannot tech up.

tier1.note: Un-killable wood floor buys the entire tier-1 army + all economy indefinitely — keeps 'floor' a true floor (§04). techWindow: start.

tier2.note: tier-2 production structures (vehicle bays / advanced-vehicle tech) need credits + ~25% of their credit-equivalent value paid in ore.

tier3.note: tier-3 tech (aircraft/epic assembly/superweapon facility) + key upgrades need credits + ~40% ore component — the top of the tech tree is the most ore-hungry, so holding an ore node is what buys the ceiling.

oreComponentFraction._note: Share of an item's credit-equivalent cost that must be paid in refined ore. Tuning values, pending the live-economy pass (see openQuestions). Chosen so the wood floor sustains tier-1 + economy but cannot reach tier-2/3 without an ore node.

oreTechGate.consistencyWithTimings: tier gates mirror timings.json techWindows exactly (tier2 3.5-6.0 min, tier3 7.0-11.0 min). Ore-gating does NOT move the windows — it makes REACHING them require the contested resource. A player can still rush a window early via economic sacrifice (timings.json _note), but doing so on wood alone is impossible past tier-1.

rosterGatherers._note: Every faction fields both a wood gatherer and an ore gatherer (in data/units/*.json), flavored per faction but sharing the canonical cost/cr-s below. Verified by scripts/economy-check.mjs (roster cross-check).

openQuestions: RESOLVED — ore tech-gating: ore is a SOFT tech-gate (both resources credit-convertible; tier-2/3 structures + key upgrades additionally require an ore component; tier-1 + economy need only the wood floor). See oreTechGate above and design/04-economy.md. Was flagged as an open question; adopted per design/18-feature-research §3 (SC2 minerals/gas model).

Exact regrow rate for wood and depletion rate for ore, plus the oreComponentFraction tuning values (tier2 0.25 / tier3 0.4), need a live-economy pass to confirm they land inside the §11 income curve (economy.json incomeCurveCreditsPerMin) across a full match.
